candidates.title: check-ci-status-dead-crons.mjs gate (hasDeadCron local observability)
candidates.why: The ci-status-beacon.yml now emits hasDeadCron + scheduledWorkflows[] to api/ci-status.json (S224). A gate that reads this file locally closes the observability gap: it makes dead crons actionable in build:check without needing GitHub access. The beacon data is already there — a gate turns a hidden signal into a blocking (advisory) local alert. Prevents the class where a cron dies for 7 runs before anyone notices (the S222 incident).

candidates.title: check-playwright-locator-all.mjs — scan for .all() + async attribute race
candidates.why: page.locator().all() followed by async getAttribute/textContent in a for-of loop is a race condition: elements can detach between collection and attribute access on dynamic pages (the S224 accessibility.spec.js bug). S224 fixed one instance by switching to page.evaluate(); a gate prevents the class from being re-introduced anywhere in the 34 spec files. This directly improves test suite reliability and prevents future CI failures from the same class.
candidates.recipe: Build scripts/check-playwright-locator-all.mjs: scan tests/*.spec.js for .all() (locator pattern) followed within 5 lines by await [...].getAttribute/textContent/innerText in a for-of. Flag with fix suggestion (use page.evaluate snapshot). Self-test 3/3. Wire into smoke-startup-scripts.

L1.recipe: Regex scan for .all() + suggest manual audit

L2.recipe: Full AST-free pattern scan: .all() within 5 lines of .getAttribute/.textContent in for-of + self-test + smoke

L3.recipe: L2 + auto-suggest page.evaluate replacement in error output

candidates.verifyNote: S224 TASK_BOARD: 'check-playwright-locator-all gate — .all() followed by async getAttribute() is a latent race condition'

candidates.title: Generalize workflow cache-dependency lint (setup-node cache: without lockfile)
candidates.why: check-workflow-install-consistency currently flags literal `cache: 'npm'` in workflows without a committed lockfile. But any `actions/setup-node` with `cache: yarn` or `cache: pnpm` suffers the same failure mode. Generalizing closes the class for all package managers — not just npm — preventing a future developer from adding a pnpm workflow that fails silently. The S221 brainstorm explicitly named this as the carry.
candidates.recipe: Extend check-workflow-install-consistency.mjs: change the lockfile-check logic to detect any cache: key (npm/yarn/pnpm/bun) in setup-node and verify the corresponding lockfile exists. Update self-test to cover yarn and pnpm cases.

L1.recipe: Add yarn/pnpm/bun to the existing npm check in check-workflow-install-consistency.mjs

L2.recipe: L1 + update self-test to cover all 4 managers + integration test against workflows/*.yml

L3.recipe: L2 + check for setup-node `cache:` without a corresponding lockfile-existence check (not just committed)

candidates.verifyNote: S221 TASK_BOARD: 'workflow cache-dependency lint. Generalize check-workflow-install-consistency to flag any setup-node cache: without committed lockfile'
